answer: When a gale damages a wharf and a terrace, a relief fund gives each resident one grant through their agent. Supervised in-person ceremonies check attendance at the same instant and issue one signed credential per person. A proof derives a campaign-specific nullifier from that credential; a shared ledger pays it once across all agent accounts. Replaying, lending or selling the credential cannot create another grant. Extra grants require recruiting more eligible people. This assumes coordinated ceremonies and honest registrars checking residency; bribed participants can still collude.
